launch-la-new-orleans-new-orleans-city-p.description: The free Besthoff Sculpture Garden pairs more than 90 works with lagoons, bridges, mature landscape, shaded paths, and entrances beside NOMA.
Storyland is a separately ticketed, seasonal storybook play environment; confirm opening hours, weather status, admission, and the restored Dragon Slide.
Carousel Gardens is a seasonal ticketed amusement area with the historic wooden carousel, rides, concessions, queues, and weather-dependent operations.
Couturie Forest and Scout Island provide free woodland trails and Laborde Mountain, New Orleans' highest point, with mud, roots, insects, and limited services.
Big Lake offers a free paved loop, fishing edges, lawns, views, and separately operated boat or bike rentals near the south cultural core.
Louisiana Children's Museum is a separately ticketed indoor-outdoor attraction with its own hours, free parking, cafe, water play, and family facilities.
New Orleans Botanical Garden is a separately scheduled and ticketed living collection with accessible paths, conservatory spaces, events, and restrooms.
Cafe du Monde serves beignets and drinks near playgrounds and lagoons on an independent schedule; queues and seating vary with crowds and weather.

launch-la-new-orleans-audubon-park.description: The popular paved loop circles the lagoon and golf course under live oaks and is shared by walkers, runners, strollers, and cyclists.
Audubon Riverview, locally called The Fly, is the Mississippi-side lawn and picnic area reached beyond the zoo, with ships, sunsets, sports, heat, and limited shade.
The free marsh-themed Riverview playground provides inclusive play near The Fly; verify surface heat, restroom access, and any posted maintenance notice.
Audubon Zoo is a separately ticketed attraction with independent gates, hours, parking, food, restrooms, animal programs, and seasonal Cool Zoo access.
The small public labyrinth near the Newman Bandstand offers quiet walking and reflection; events and wet ground can affect access.
Reservable shelters and picnic areas are distributed across the park and Riverview; a reservation controls organized use, not the surrounding public landscape.
Audubon Park Golf Course occupies the center of the loop and has separate tee times, fees, clubhouse access, and safety boundaries.
Ochsner Island is a protected rookery in the lagoon viewed from shore; visitors must not enter, feed birds, launch boats, or disturb nesting habitat.

launch-la-new-orleans-crescent-park.description: Mandeville Wharf is the broad central event lawn and covered industrial structure with river views, art, paths, and flexible gathering space.
Piety Wharf and its overlook are reached by the Rusty Rainbow bridge system and provide dramatic skyline, ship, and sunset views.
The Rusty Rainbow is a steep arched pedestrian bridge over active rail lines, with both stairs and a long ramp but significant elevation.
Mazant Street provides a lower-key Bywater approach near the eastern park sections; verify gate access and legal neighborhood parking.
Bartholomew Street is the eastern end access and useful turnaround, but offers fewer nearby visitor services than the Marigny end.
The fenced dog run provides designated off-leash space; dogs must be leashed immediately outside and need water during hot weather.
Open-sided pavilions provide shade and event space along the exposed riverfront but may be reserved or affected by weather.
River overlooks face working Mississippi traffic, skyline, bridges, and sunsets; railings do not replace direct child supervision.

launch-la-new-orleans-louis-armstrong-pa.description: Congo Square is the park's nationally significant gathering ground and a living center of African diasporic music, dance, ceremony, markets, and public memory.
Mahalia Jackson Theater is a separately operated performance venue with controlled entrances, ticketing, security, restrooms, and event parking.
The Municipal Auditorium is a major historic building within the landscape but should not be assumed open; follow current redevelopment and closure notices.
Perseverance Hall is a historic jazz and mutual-aid landmark whose exterior can be appreciated even when the building is not open to visitors.
Arched bridges and paths cross decorative lagoons through the park; water is not for swimming and surfaces can be slick after rain.
The Louis Armstrong statue is one of several music memorials and a useful orientation point along the central paths.
The Sidney Bechet statue honors the New Orleans clarinetist and sits within a broader sculpture walk devoted to the city's musicians.
The North Rampart arch is the clearest general gateway from the French Quarter and streetcar corridor, but event screening may redirect entry.

launch-la-new-orleans-lafitte-greenway.description: Lemann Playground is a NORD recreation node beside the greenway with play, fields, pool or program facilities on separate seasonal schedules.
Greenway Plaza near North Norman C. Francis is a gathering and event area connected to nearby food, gardens, transit, and the shared-use path.
Public basketball courts support free play when not programmed or closed; bring your own ball and yield to scheduled activities.
FitLot provides free outdoor fitness equipment and occasional coached programs; surfaces and equipment can become dangerously hot.
The Bayou St. John trailhead links the greenway with the bayou, City Park approaches, neighborhood biking, and longer routes.
North Claiborne is the downtown-side trail approach toward Tremé and Armstrong Park, with a major street crossing requiring attention.
Bioswales and planted stormwater areas manage rainfall and habitat; they are not play channels and can hold water after storms.
Murals, sculpture, and temporary installations appear along the corridor; explore slowly without blocking commuting cyclists and runners.

launch-la-new-orleans-goldring-woldenber.description: The 2026 Governor Nicholls expansion adds a free Louisiana marsh-themed playground, shaded seating, cooling misters, lawns, and direct St. Philip Street access.
The covered NOLA Front Porch is a large open-air community and event space overlooking the river; programmed events may change casual access.
The Moonwalk is the classic French Quarter river promenade between Jackson Square and the downtown waterfront, with steps, ships, performers, and little shade.
Spanish Plaza anchors the Canal Street end near the Aquarium, ferry, transit, food, fountains, and paid downtown parking.
The riverside Holocaust Memorial combines sculpture and optical panels in a contemplative setting; supervise children and treat it respectfully.
The Aquarium plaza is public riverfront space outside a separately ticketed attraction with its own hours, security, restrooms, and food.
The Canal Street ferry landing connects downtown with Algiers Point on an operating schedule affected by weather, river conditions, and service changes.
The Bienville Street overlook provides river and vessel views near the central tourist district, with crowds and event activity varying sharply.

launch-la-new-orleans-jackson-square.description: The equestrian Andrew Jackson monument anchors the gated garden; lawns and the statue base are not climbing or play equipment.
The Chartres Street side faces St. Louis Cathedral, an active place of worship with independent opening, service, dress, and photography rules.
The Cabildo is a separately ticketed Louisiana State Museum beside the square with its own entrance, hours, security, and accessible route.
The Presbytère is a separately ticketed state museum focused on Mardi Gras and Hurricane Katrina, with independent visitor operations.
Washington Artillery Park is the elevated public terrace across Decatur Street, providing the classic cathedral-and-square view and river access.
The Moonwalk overlook connects the square area to the Mississippi River, steamboat views, levee steps, and the broader riverfront park.
Artists and performers typically work around the square's outer Decatur and Chartres edges; portraits, tips, tours, and carriage rides are private transactions.
The St. Ann Street gate provides a quieter side approach but closes with the formal garden's posted daily schedule.

launch-la-new-orleans-bayou-sauvage-urba.description: The half-mile Ridge Trail interpretive boardwalk, restroom, and pavilion have been closed since March 2, 2026 for boardwalk reconstruction; do not route here without checking reopening status.
Maxent Levee allows walking and bicycling through open refuge habitat from the Ridge Trail area, subject to gates, construction, weather, and seasonal rules.
Joe Madere Marsh provides wetland observation and fishing access in remote exposed habitat where water, shade, restrooms, and mobile service cannot be assumed.
The Highway 11 launch and small fishing pier access canals toward Lake Maisson and Lake Antoine; boating safety and Louisiana rules apply.
Irish Bayou access serves fishing and boating near the refuge edge; verify launch conditions, gates, weather, and exact navigation before departure.
Fishing and crabbing are allowed in designated waters under current Louisiana and refuge rules, with seasonal restrictions outside the protection levee.
Marsh, forest, lagoon, and open-water habitats support alligators and abundant birds; observe from distance and never feed wildlife.
Access outside the Hurricane Protection Levee is delayed until noon during teal season and November 1-January 31; posted gates always control.
